messages:
maya: quick note: building a new Next agent starter that wires Redwood SDK + LangChain. hit an auth/refresh parity problem between node and edge bundles.
jordan: brief?
maya: in node, when token expires the SDK triggers refresh and retries. in edge/browser bundle the retry sends the original request object and the Authorization header gets lost on redirect so it never retries properly.
sam: can you share the failing stack?
maya: pasted below:
```
FetchError: 401 Unauthorized
    at fetchWrapper (packages/sdk/dist/edge.js:85:12)
    at process (internal/task.js:45:3)
```
chloe: is this the starter repo or your personal example?
maya: starter: github.com/redwood-inference/next-agent-starter (internal). README currently tells users to set REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env.local. our eval-harness docs show ephemeral refresh flowsusers get confused which pattern to use.
jordan: repro steps?
maya: minimal repro: start dev, hit /agent page, then rotate the key on the backend to force 401. I put a tiny script in the repo to expire tokens quickly.
devex-bot: CI alert: e2e job failing on PR #317, snapshot mismatch for /agent page.
sam: dug in: the retry code clones the Request but doesn't reattach runtime headers from the token store. Edge fetch implementations sometimes drop manually set headers on redirected requests. quick fix: when retrying, rebuild the request with fresh headers from token storage instead of reusing the old request.headers object.
chloe: agree. also we should update the starter README to document two modes: "local static key" vs "ephemeral refresh server". onboarding notes should call out tradeoffs.
jordan: can we add an automated test to the starter that fakes token expiry and asserts the retry path ends in success? recommend msw + jest fake timers.
maya: will add a test. planning to mock the refresh endpoint and assert the final call includes the new Authorization header.
sam: PR #320 opened with the retry change and a failing flaky test. flakiness due to real timers and network scheduling.
jordan: use jest.useFakeTimers() and advanceTimersByTime to make it deterministic. also add a metric like sdk.auth_retry_count so we can detect regressions.
maya: added the metric and switched to fake timers, updated README with a short section on token strategies.
chloe: after this merges let's port the fix to other sample apps (vite-react starter, edge-samplekit). new hires keep tripping on this when following the quickstart.
devex-bot: CI: PR #320 passed checks (build 6521) :white_check_mark:
maya: thanks all 44d merging now. i'll also drop a message in #devex-docs with a short troubleshooting blurb and the test case so teams can copy it.
jordan: solid. also consider adding a short entry in the eval-harness runbook that shows how to reproduce token rotation locally and which traces to look for.
maya: good idea, i'll add that next week.
